candidate.answerReason: The units digits repeat as \(3,9,7,1\). Since \(2003=4\cdot500+3\), the requested digit is the third digit in the cycle.

methods.label: Track the repeating units digits
methods.explanation:
The units digit of a product depends only on the units digits of its factors, because all other place-value contributions are multiples of \(10\). Thus multiplying by \(13\) changes the units digit just as multiplying by \(3\) does.

Starting with \(13^1\), the successive units digits are
\[
3,\quad9,\quad7,\quad1.
\]
The next multiplication gives units digit \(3\) again. Since each next digit is determined by the preceding digit, the same four-digit cycle repeats indefinitely.

Now
\[
2003=4\cdot500+3.
\]
After \(500\) complete cycles, the exponent is three positions into the next cycle. The third digit is \(\boxed{7}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{C}}\).
methods.levelReason: The solution uses decimal place value and division with remainder to justify and locate a units-digit cycle, without formal congruence notation or exponent theorems.
